newsitem.title: UK: Media consolidation to help advertising - executive.
newsitem.headline: Media consolidation to help advertising - executive.

text.p: The consolidation of media ownership in recent years will have a positive impact on the advertising industry and advertisers, a senior industry executive said on Thursday.
Brian Jacobs, managing director of Carat International, told a business conference that as media owners get bigger so do the benefits they can offer advertisers.
He cited New York-based Time Warner Inc as an example of a media and communications giant that could offer advertisers powerful new channels to consumers.

"(Time Warner's) subscriber database expertise is impressive and could lead to the personalising of ads in Time magazine," Jacobs told the second Media International Objective Research Conference in London.
He said Time Warner, whose holdings include Turner Networks and Warner Music Group, could use its powerful subscriber database to customise advertising to target different consumer groups.
"The most appropriate ad could be put in front of the reader. A car manufacturer could advertise an estate car to families or a sports coupe to single young adults," Jacobs said.
"The ad could even be personalised to the individual reader mentioning him or her by name", he said.
Carat International, which is owned by London-based Aegis Group Plc, is Europe's biggest media planning and buying network.
Jacobs described Rupert Murdoch's News Corporation, NBC and Bertelsmann AG in Germany as other multimedia giants that offered advertisers new links to consumers.

In the case of Time Warner, he said advertisers could benefit from the group's multi-media interests by linkin advertising to incentives such as Warner records and videos and Time publications. They could also link their Websites to Time Warner's Website.
Jacobs said the distinction between advertising and editorial was becoming increasing blurred.
"I think the process has already begun. What is advertising? Are phone directories advertising? Are magazines produced by retail groups advertising?" he said.

"And more to the point does it matter? The learning from the U.S., where advertiser-supplied programmes and sponsorship are common means of promotion, is: be subtle, be tasteful, be appropriate, be relevant or die", Jacobs said.
